title: Modular in vivo antibody-ADC click to reverse drug resistance in tumours.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the 152 KB source-data Excel workbook (MOESM4): 28 sheets, one per figure panel, 2,796 non-empty rows total. Counted unique mice per tumour-growth sheet: 13, 54, 48, 19, 56, 48 and 30 animals, i.e. roughly 164 distinct mice once the duplicated sheets are removed (Figure 4b shares 85 identical rows with Ext. Figure 3a; Figure 4e shares 172 with Ext. Figure 3b). Confirmed the growth sheets carry only Group (0-4 treatment arm), Mouse ID, Gender, Day and Tumor fold-change. Also HEAD-probed MOESM1-14 and found only three PDFs plus this one workbook. Confirmed licence is CC BY-NC-ND from Europe PMC metadata.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the immunohistochemistry (antibody staining of tissue slices) images were co-registered and scored by automated image analysis, and the Dice similarity coefficient values of 0.12 and 0.26 for HER2/EGFR spatial overlap. The underlying whole-slide images, the per-tile segmentation output and the co-registration code are not in any file I could retrieve. The Europe PMC supplementaryFiles endpoint failed twice (killed at 75 s), so the Supplementary Information PDFs' internal table contents were not opened.

a1_downloadable.note: Source data workbook downloaded with no login from the publisher's static file host (152 KB, opened and parsed). But the only data that exists is this figure-panel workbook: no repository deposit (no GEO, SRA, Zenodo, figshare or GitHub anywhere in the text), and the statement says to contact the corresponding author for further assistance.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Passes only in the narrowest sense: 'Tumor fold-change' and 'Survival status'/'Days' are literal columns in the growth and survival sheets. There is no feature side to pair them with - the only predictors present are a treatment-arm code 0-4, sex, day and mouse ID.

a3_inputs_present.note: There are no model inputs at all. Treatment arm is a categorical code (0=saline, 1=panitumumab, 2=T-DXd, ...) with no molecular representation; the antibody and drug-conjugate structures are described in prose and figure panels, not as sequences or SMILES strings. The images that could have been inputs (the HER2/EGFR stained tissue sections) were never deposited.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated and consistent where they appear: %ID/g and %ID/mL for radiotracer uptake, tumour fold-change relative to day 0, days for survival, and U/L-style liver enzyme values (ALT/AST/ALP). Verified in the sheet headers.

a5_enough_rows.note: KILLER. The experimental unit is the mouse. I counted roughly 164 distinct animals across the five non-redundant tumour-growth studies (largest single study = 56 mice split over 5 arms, i.e. 9-14 per arm), plus a few dozen more in the PET and biodistribution sheets of 3-4 mice each. The checklist needs ~1,500 labelled rows, or ~400 for classification. The 2,796 spreadsheet rows are repeated caliper measurements of the same ~164 animals over 10-17 timepoints, not independent examples.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits; the problem is the opposite of size.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Consistent. The text quotes n = 2-14 mice per group (most commonly 3, 4, 9 or 10); the workbook's per-arm counts of 9-14 for growth studies and 3-4 for imaging match that. No contradictory totals found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels are direct physical measurements: caliper tumour volume normalised to day 0, gamma-counted radioactivity per organ, survival date, and serum chemistry. Nothing is another model's output. The one model-derived quantity in the paper, the Dice overlap coefficient from automated image co-registration, is not used as a label.

existing_models.name: ADCNet (antibody-drug conjugate activity predictor, arXiv:2401.09176)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified - I retrieved only the search-result title and preprint URL, not the numbers or the split.

existing_models.name: AMM, a multimodal convolutional neural network for antibody-drug conjugate in vitro potency, trained with gene and protein data from ~1,400 human tumour cell lines (Research Square preprint rs-6256038)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified - search snippet only; reported as predicting whether potency crosses nanomolar thresholds per cell line, with no split stated in what I retrieved.

existing_models.name: Deep learning HER2 immunohistochemistry scorers (a dense literature: dual-centre scoring studies, multi-scale hierarchical graph neural networks, membrane segmentation networks)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not verified. Relevant because automated HER2 staining assessment is the one task this paper touches, and it is already a crowded, well-evaluated field with multi-centre validation.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Insufficient integration of membrane shape with cell spatial layout, and dependence on extra stains, per the retrieved abstracts.

backbone.name: None applicable
backbone.licence: Data is CC BY-NC-ND, which also discourages redistributing a derived table.

integration.partner_dataset: None viable. The five cell lines used (NCIN87, A431, MIAPaCa-2, BT474, CT26-hHER2) are named in prose, not as identifiers, and five cell lines will not join usefully to DepMap or the Cell Model Passports.
integration.join_key: Cell line name as free text; no UniProt, Ensembl or InChIKey anywhere in the workbook.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written - with five cell lines and one laboratory's dosing protocol there is no question a join would answer that the paper does not already answer with a t-test.

controls.positive_control: The saline arm versus the standard antibody-drug conjugate arm is a real internal positive control, but with 9-14 mice per arm it is a statistical comparison, not a machine-learning control.
controls.negative_control: The non-targeted IgG-DM1 control arm exists in Ext. Figure 3d (30 mice, 4 arms) - good experimental design, irrelevant at this sample size.
controls.external_validation: None. No second dataset, no publication-year column, one laboratory, one dosing schedule.

honest_claim_h3: Any model fitted to this workbook would claim only: 'in this one laboratory's hands, across five cell lines and about 164 mice, the clicked antibody-drug conjugate arm shrank tumours more than the unclicked arm' - which is a difference of means the authors already report, not a prediction.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use treatment arm, sex and receptor levels to predict how much a mouse tumour grows or shrinks.
plain_idea.train_on: What I considered: one row per mouse per measurement day, with treatment arm (saline, antibody alone, standard antibody-drug conjugate, the clicked version), sex, day and cell line. I verified there are about 164 distinct mice in total, across 2 to 5 arms per study.
plain_idea.predict: Tumour volume fold-change relative to the first day of treatment, measured with calipers on live mice, or survival time in days. Both are real columns in the source-data workbook.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: It would not be. With 9 to 14 animals per arm and four categorical predictors, the honest analysis is the mixed-effects model with Dunnett correction that the authors already ran; a machine-learning model adds nothing and would mostly memorise the arm label.

ml_idea: No viable machine-learning project. The two things that looked promising on the abstract both evaporate on the files. (1) Predicting tumour response from treatment arm: the data is roughly 164 mice in 2-5 arms, so the only predictor is a 5-level categorical code and the analysis is an ANOVA, which the authors did. (2) Predicting HER2/EGFR spatial co-expression from stained tissue images: the whole-slide images were never deposited, only two summary Dice overlap numbers (0.12 and 0.26) made it into the text, and the co-registration code is 'described in the Methods' rather than released. Automated HER2 immunohistochemistry scoring is in any case an already-crowded deep-learning field with multi-centre evaluated models.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not estimated: the workbook is 151,851 bytes and parsed in under a second with openpyxl. Three hours would cover un-pivoting the 28 wide figure-panel sheets into one long table. Compute is not the obstacle.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count unique (Group, Mouse ID) pairs in the tumour-growth sheets. I did this: 13, 54, 48, 19, 56, 48, 30 animals, with two sheet pairs being the same data replotted. About 164 independent units kills the project in five minutes.

verdict_reason: A5 fails hard, and A3 with it. This is a preclinical mouse pharmacology paper: the complete quantitative record is one 152 KB Excel workbook of 28 figure-panel sheets, and the experimental unit is the mouse - about 164 distinct animals across five non-redundant tumour-growth studies, 9 to 14 per treatment arm (verified by counting unique Group/Mouse ID pairs, with Figure 4b/Ext. Figure 3a and Figure 4e/Ext. Figure 3b sharing 85 and 172 identical rows respectively). The 2,796 spreadsheet rows are repeated caliper readings on the same animals, not independent examples. There is also no input side: treatment is a categorical code 0-4 with no molecular representation, and the stained tissue images that could have been modelled were never deposited (no repository accession anywhere in the text, and the co-registration code is described rather than released). Counts match the paper and units are clean, so the data is honest and well kept - it is simply a hypothesis-testing dataset, not a training set.
